Ucraina colpisce il ponte di Crimea: le immagini mostrano un'arcata crollata in mare.

Secondo il Guardian una campata stradale di 227 metri è caduta nello stretto di Kerch. Il traffico su strada e ferrovia è sospeso, ma il ministero dei Trasporti russo non conferma il crollo. Zelensky parla di un'operazione in sette fasi, il Cremlino promette di ricostruire il ponte. Nella stessa notte la Russia ha colpito due ponti di Kiev.

Che conseguenze avrà sulle trattative, a pochi giorni dal vertice di Shenzhen?

c.titolo_copertina: Ponte di Crimea colpito dall'Ucraina: le immagini mostrano un'arcata crollata in mare

slide.titolo: Droni e missili sul ponte di Kerch
slide.testo: Nella notte di martedì 17 novembre l'Ucraina ha colpito il ponte tra Russia e Crimea occupata. Zelensky parla di operazione "senza precedenti". Mosca ha sospeso il traffico stradale e ferroviario. Il ministero dei Trasporti russo non conferma il crollo.

Secondo le foto citate dal Guardian, è la campata ad arco crollata. I danni non sono verificati in modo indipendente. I detriti potrebbero bloccare il canale navigabile verso i porti di Mariupol e Berdiansk.

Secondo Zelensky, per settimane le forze ucraine hanno distrutto difese aeree, radar e sistemi di guerra elettronica. Poi l'attacco finale: droni Palianytsia sulla strada, missili Neptune e droni sulla ferrovia, più un missile da crociera Flamingo.
Non c'è dubbio che il ponte sarà ripristinato e sarà ancora migliore di prima.

slide.titolo: La Russia colpisce due ponti sul Dnipro
slide.testo: Chiusi i ponti Nord e Sud della capitale ucraina, riferisce il sindaco Vitali Klitschko. Danni alle infrastrutture critiche, interruzioni di acqua, riscaldamento ed elettricità. Secondo la BBC, circa tre milioni di residenti usano i ponti per attraversare la città.

slide.titolo: Crimea più isolata, vertice in vista
slide.testo: Restano il corridoio terrestre nel sud occupato, bersagliato dai droni, e un traghetto a capacità limitata. Il canale filorusso Rybar ammette che riparare il ponte sarà difficile. Giovedì Putin incontra Trump e Xi a Shenzhen.

c.perche_ti_riguarda: Per ora non ci sono effetti diretti sull'Italia. L'attacco però arriva mentre negoziatori ucraini, europei e statunitensi discutono di futuri colloqui con la Russia, alla vigilia del vertice Putin-Trump-Xi. L'esito della guerra pesa sulla sicurezza europea.

sources.title: Crimean Bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine
sources.text:
Crimean Bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine
- Published
Ukraine has severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, in what Volodymyr Zelensky says was an "unprecedented operation" weeks in the making.
Images shared by Ukrainian officials show a section of the Crimean Bridge - also known as the Kerch Bridge - has collapsed into the water, dealing a logistical and symbolic blow to Russia's war effort.
A Kremlin spokesperson insisted the bridge would be rebuilt "better than before".
Elsewhere, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the Northern and Southern bridges, both important crossings over the Dnipro River, were closed after Russia targeted the Ukrainian capital overnight.
Ukraine has long targeted the Crimean Bridge, which provides a road and rail route for Russian soldiers heading towards the front line, but has struggled to close it for good.
The damage reported on Tuesday appeared to be far more severe than previously, with a large arched section of the bridge apparently destroyed.
Video footage appeared to show critical damage to the road section, with remnants of the support arch and road deck seen protruding from the water below.
Zelensky said the overnight strike was the result of a seven-stage operation by the military and security services, which saw Ukrainian forces "gradually destroy air defence systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment, and other designated targets on the way to the final objective".
He said the rail section parallel to the bridge's road had also been hit by a wave of drones, though images showed its supporting arch was still standing and a Russian-backed official said some rail services were operating.
The bridge was built by Russia after it invaded and annexed the peninsula in 2014, and was personally opened by Russian President Vladimir Putin in 2018.
While Ukraine has been trying to increase the cost to Russia of waging war economically, by hitting oil refineries and depots, striking the bridge is an attempt to increase the political cost on Putin.
The timing of the strike comes at a significant moment, ahead of Putin meeting the leaders of China and the US. This could cloud his moment back in the spotlight.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge would "be restored following Ukrainian strikes, and it will be even better than before", and did not rule out the possibility the strikes were linked to Putin's visit to china.
Russia's Investigative Committee confirmed structural damage and said it had opened a "criminal case... on terrorism charges" after attacks by "Ukraine's armed formations".
For the second day in a row, Russia recorded the biggest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, with 2,256 drones downed, according to the defence ministry.
Zelensky had warned of major attacks in the days leading up to a meeting between Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in China's Shenzhen on Thursday.
Loud explosions were heard in Kyiv just before midnight on Tuesday, with Klitschko saying shortly after that the city had suffered "damage to critical infrastructure systems" and disruption to heating and water.
Some of Kyiv's above-ground subway services were damaged in the overnight attacks, officials said, after civilians were told to go to civil defence shelters.
Eight major bridges span the Dnipro River connecting the western and eastern parts of Kyiv, and an estimated three million residents rely on the bridges to travel across the city.
Strikes on the busy Northern and Southern Bridges will cause major disruption to people's daily lives.
Elsewhere, three people have been injured in a Russian missile attack in the Cherkast region, according to local officials.
The long-term impact of the Crimean Bridge strike is still not fully clear though the risk of a serious transport and logistics crisis for the Russian military has increased significantly.
The collapse of the arched section of the Crimean Bridge has cut off the peninsula's direct road and rail links with Russia â at least until the crossing can be repaired.
However, there is still a land corridor running through the occupied parts of the Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions - though Ukraine has been systematically striking transport routes across northern Crimea, as well as bridges and other crossings in the area around Chongar.
This has already caused problems with the delivery of fuel and other supplies, including military cargo.
There is a ferry crossing across the Kerch Strait. It could partly compensate for the loss of the bridge, but its capacity is very limited and it is also vulnerable to attack.
Russia could also supply Crimea by sea, but this route is also risky, as Ukrainian naval and aerial drones operate extensively in the area.
In addition, debris from the Crimean Bridge â particularly its enormous arch â may have blocked the shipping channel.
This would make it harder for larger vessels to pass through and create further problems for ports in the Sea of Azov, including Mariupol and Berdiansk.
Russia's launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Approximately one-fifth of Ukraine is now under Russian occupation and Kyiv has refused Putin's demand to give up areas of Ukraine's eastern Donbas that remain under its control.

sources.title: Ukraine critically damages Kerch bridge linking occupied Crimea with Russia
sources.text:
Ukraine has critically damaged the Kerch bridge linking occupied Crimea with Russia in an overnight missile attack, in what Volodymyr Zelenskyy hailed as an “unprecedented” military operation.
Footage showed a Ukrainian Flamingo cruise missile seconds before it hit the road and railway crossing, followed by an explosion. The strike follows an earlier attack on Monday that targeted an arch across its central section.
Writing on social media, the Ukrainian president described the attack as “a response to Russian strikes on our infrastructure”. He said it was the culmination of a long and complex campaign to demolish the bridge, involving domestically produced drones and ballistic missiles.
“Our warriors gradually destroyed air defence systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment, and other designated targets on the way to the final objective,” he wrote. Palianytsia drones hit the road section of the bridge, while Neptune and other missiles targeted the adjacent rail section, he added.
Earlier, Russian forces struck two major bridges in Kyiv that straddle the Dnipro River late on Monday, along with some other critical infrastructure, amid drone and missile attacks across Ukraine.
Ukraine has declared that the Kerch bridge, built eight years ago after Vladimir Putin’s 2014 annexation of Crimea and known officially as the Crimean Bridge, is illegal. It has repeatedly attempted to destroy it, using a truck bomb in 2022 and a sea drone strike the following year.
The latest drone and missile barrage appears to have succeeded after months in which Ukrainian unmanned systems forces have systematically knocked out the peninsula’s multi-layered air defences.
The Kremlin-appointed governor of Crimea, Sergey Aksyonov, confirmed that the bridge, which was temporarily closed on Monday, was no longer usable. “The enemy has once again attacked the Crimean Bridge. At the moment, traffic has been suspended,” he posted on Telegram.
He added: “We ask residents and visitors in Crimea to refrain from travelling toward the bridge and to take these restrictions into account when planning their routes.”
Photos on Tuesday suggest that a 227-metre road arch span has fallen into the Kerch strait, which connects the Sea of Azov with the Black Sea. The adjacent railway arch span has also sustained damage.
Ukrainian commentators say the massive steel arch cannot easily be replaced. The closure of the bridge means traffic from Crimea can travel out of the peninsula only via a land corridor through occupied southern Ukraine, vulnerable to Ukrainian drones.
The debris appears to have blocked the main navigable route beneath the bridge, used by maritime traffic from the Sea of Azov and the ports of Berdiansk and Mariupol. The channel is 120 metres wide and 8.3 metres deep. Submerged steel struts could prevent large vessels from passing until the debris is removed.
The Russian government convened an emergency meeting to assess the attack, after which one of the country’s deputy prime ministers, Marat Khusnullin, briefed Putin on the damage to the bridge, according to the Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov.
Peskov added that the bridge would be repaired and would be “even better than before”, in comments to the Russian newspaper Izvestia.
But pro-war Russian commentators acknowledged that repairing the bridge would be very difficult, warning that, unlike in 2022 and 2023, Ukraine now had the capability to strike floating cranes and repair crews.
“Even installing a prefabricated arch under such conditions would be a formidable challenge,” wrote the influential Rybar Telegram channel, with close links to the defence ministry.
Ukrainian observers were gleeful at the bridge’s long-awaited destruction. They also pointed out that Ukraine’s armed forces could hit the bridge again to prevent repair work from being carried out. Serhii Sternenko, a former adviser to the defence ministry in Kyiv, wrote: “In response to your many questions. Yes, the bridge is fucked.”
The Ukrainian blogger Anton Gerashchenko pointed out that Putin personally opened the bridge in 2018, driving across it in a Kamaz truck. “The Kerch bridge stands as the primary symbol of the Russian occupation of Ukrainian Crimea and the embodiment of its illegal annexation. It is Putin’s flagship project,” he wrote.
He added: “For years, Russian authorities claimed the bridge was ‘the most protected facility in the world’. Consequently, every successful strike shatters the myth of the invincibility of Russian air defences – as well as the notion that Ukraine is incapable of reaching key targets deep behind enemy lines.”
Ukrainians celebrated on Tuesday with memes. The company Fire Point, which manufactures the Flamingo missile, posted a popcorn emoji. Other social media users shared video of “Kerch Bridge on Fire”, a popular song by Saint Javelin which has become an anti-Moscow anthem.
Russian military bloggers were gloomy. One, Russian Engineer, acknowledged the Ukrainian military operation to paralyse the bridge had been “perfect”. Hundreds of unmanned aerial vehicles distracted Russian air defences, he said, before a clinical strike by ballistic missiles.
The attack will further complicate supplies to Crimea, after a summer in which the peninsula struggled with fuel shortages and an intensifying Ukrainian campaign to isolate it from mainland Russia.
Ukraine has for months focused its strikes on the key transport routes supplying Crimea, particularly the so-called Novorossiya highway, a key logistics corridor linking the peninsula to Russia’s Rostov region through the occupied cities of Melitopol and Mariupol.
Russia had already sharply restricted traffic across the Crimean bridge. Moscow has largely stopped using the crossing for rail fuel shipments since the 2022 Ukrainian attack damaged the bridge and set a fuel train ablaze.
Rybar wrote that the latest strike would force Moscow to “completely overhaul” its supply routes to Crimea, shifting more traffic to the Novor

sources.title: Ukraine updates: Russia-Crimea bridge appears destroyed after strike
sources.text:
Ukraine updates: Russia-Crimea bridge appears destroyed after strike
Published November 17, 2026last updated November 17, 2026
What you need to know
- Ukraine strike hits Kerch bridge connecting occupied Crimea to the Russian mainland, stopping traffic
- Images show part of the bridge destroyed
- Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the strike on Kerch bridge an 'unprecedented operation'
- Russia also struck two important bridges in Kyiv, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said
- The attacks come as Ukrainian, European and US negotiators discuss future talks with Russia on ending the war
These are the main developments from Russia's war in Ukraine on November 17, 2026:
IN PICTURES: Kerch bridge strike
Vladimir Putin briefed on Kerch bridge strike — Russian media
Russia state media has reported that President Vladimir Putin has been briefed by Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin "on the situation around the Crimean Bridge," citing Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov.
"Following the government commission meeting, Marat Khusnullin reported to President Putin on the situation surrounding the Crimean Bridge," Peskov told reporters.
"According to the Investigative Committee, on November 16 and 17, Ukrainian armed forces attacked the Crimean Bridge using unmanned aerial vehicle, resulting in damage to the structure," TASS reported.
Russian media also quoted Peskov as saying that the bridge linking occupied Crimea with mainland Russia would be "even better" after it was restored, giving an indication as to the extent of the damage caused.
"There is, of course, no doubt that the bridge will be restored and will be even better than before," Peskov said, quoted by Russian state media.
Ukraine's Zelenskyy confirms strike on Kerch bridge
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has confirmed that the Kerch bridge was targeted by Ukrainian forces, describing it as "an unprecedented operation in response to Russian strikes on our infrastructure."
"Today, everyone can see the consequences for the main military crossing from Russian territory into our Ukrainian Crimea," Zelenskyy said in a lengthy post on social media platform X.
The Ukrainian leader said the strike was a culmination of an operation "carried out over several weeks" by his country's military and involved destroying air defense systems, radar systems and electronic warfare equipment in the lead up to the attack.
Zelenskyy said that the road section of the bridge was hit by "Palianytsia" drones and while the railway section was targeted by "Neptune" missiles and "Ruta" drones.
"We have repeatedly offered Russia steps toward de-escalation — and every proposal has been met with loud rejection," Zelenskyy said and pointed to continued Russian strikes on Ukraine's infrastructure.
His post was accompanied by footage appearing to show the moment the bridge was struck and then the subsequent aftermath with one part of the bridge collapsed.
Germany and Norway to purchase more air defenses for Ukraine
Germany and Norway will fund a new US air defense package for Ukraine's defensive needs, according to Germany's defense chief.
"Russia is intensifying its air attacks because it is not making progress on the battlefield," Defense Minister Boris Pistorius said at an EU meeting in Brussels.
Pistorius said that Germany would contribute $300 million (€272 million) towards the weapons package that would include Patriot interceptor missiles.
The package will also include previously announced IRIS-T systems, as well as new radars and ammunition for F-16 fighter jets and drones.
The announcement comes ahead of a meeting of Ukraine's military backers at NATO headquarters in Brussels later today.
Germany has, since the start of Russia's invasion, provided civilian aid totalling more than €45.7 billion and provided or earmarked military aid of around €57.8 billion, according to the German government.
Power outages in 9 Ukrainian regions after Russian strikes — energy official
Ukraine's Deputy Energy Minister Artem Nekrasov, said that Russian strikes on energy infrastructure had caused power outages in nine Ukrainian regions.
"As a result of the strikes, some consumers have been left without electricity in the Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, Mykolaiv, Odesa, Rivne, Sumy, Chernihiv and Chernivtsi regions," Nekrasov said.
"The situation is extremely difficult in the Dnipropetrovsk and Zaporizhzhia regions. Since last week, Russia has been continuously attacking energy facilities in the Dnipro region," Nekrasov said.
Russian government talks to be held after Kerch strike — Russian media
A government meeting is expected to take place soon following the strike on the Kerch bridge, Russian state media agency TASS reported.
"A meeting of the government commission on the aftermath of the attack on the Crimean Bridge, chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin, will be held soon at Government House," TASS quoted the Russian government as saying.
"The meeting will address issues related to the restoration of the Crimean Bridge and the organization of transport links," TASS reported.
The extent of the damage caused is not yet known and Russian officials have only confirmed that a strike had taken place and that traffic has been disrupted.
Crimea strike kills 2, says Russia-installed governor
A drone strike on Crimea has killed two people, according to the Russia-installed governor Sergei Aksyonov.
He said on Telegram that the strike took place in the Leninsky district of Crimea, which was seized and annexed from Ukraine in 2014.
Earlier Aksyonov said that Ukraine had struck the Kerch bridge, causing traffic to be suspended.
Moscow built the Kerch Bridge to link the annexed Crimean Peninsula to the Russian region of Krasnodar Krai in the northern Caucasus.
The route is a major source of supplies for Russian forces in Ukraine's occupied Kherson region and is a strategically significant target for Ukrainian forces.

sources.title: How Ukrainian forces struck Putin's prized and heavily defended Crimean bridge
sources.text:
Ukraine's unprecedented seven-stage operation reportedly partially destroyed one of Russia's most heavily defended infrastructure sites, a vital military supply route to occupied Crimea and the crown jewel of Vladimir Putin's occupation of the peninsula.
Ukrainian forces used a combination of drones and missiles to strike the road and railway sections of the Crimean Bridge overnight into Tuesday, following weeks of coordinated attacks aimed at dismantling Russian air defences protecting the crossing.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy revealed details of the strike, which marked the culmination of a seven-stage operation developed and coordinated by Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) and the General Staff of the Armed Forces, involving 11 different weapons systems.
Images circulating after the attack appeared to show one of the bridge's main arches and part of its roadway collapsed into the sea, potentially dealing a major blow to the crossing linking Russia with occupied Crimea.
Russia's Transport Ministry confirmed that both road and rail traffic had been suspended following a second consecutive day of attacks, but did not confirm the reported collapse.
How Ukraine carried out the operation
In a detailed statement published on X, Zelenskyy said Ukrainian forces had spent several weeks systematically targeting Russian military systems protecting the crossing.
"Our warriors gradually destroyed air defense systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment, and other designated targets on the way to the final objective," Zelenskyy said.
He identified eleven weapons systems used throughout the operation: Dovbush, Vendetta, Da Vinci, Sichen, Mich-2000, Ruta, Palianytsia, An-197, FP-1, FP-5 Flamingo and R-360 Neptune.
At the final stage, Ukrainian forces used different weapons to target the bridge's two transport sections.
"Today, at the key stage, the 'Palianytsia' drones performed exceptionally well, striking the road section of the bridge, while 'Neptune' missiles, 'Ruta' drones, and FP-5 drones struck the railway section," Zelenskyy said.
The Ukrainian president also highlighted the use of the FP-5 Flamingo cruise missile in a precision-guided strike.
"Using 'Flamingo,' our warriors carried out a precision-guided strike – and the communications uplink worked flawlessly until the very last seconds."
Robert Brovdi, known by his callsign "Magyar", commander of Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces, also commented on the attack, identifying several Ukrainian military units involved in the operation.
According to Brovdi, the strike was a joint operation involving deep-strike units of the Ukrainian Navy, the Rocket Forces and Artillery, the newly formed 7th Centre of the 414th "Magyar's Birds" Brigade, the 1st Centre of the Unmanned Systems Forces and Ukraine's Security Service (SBU).
"The sacred bridge is tired. It's time for rubber dinghies," Brovdi wrote.
He also suggested that the attack would have lasting consequences for Russian transport connections to the peninsula.
Fire Point, the Ukrainian manufacturer of the Flamingo cruise missile, reacted to the attack on X, posting a brief message: "Crimea is Ukraine btw."
"Crimean Bridge. Sanctioned," Ukraine's Presidential Sanctions Commissioner Vladyslav Vlasiuk wrote in a separate post on X.
Zelenskyy did not specify how many drones or missiles were launched, how many reached their targets, or which weapons were responsible for the reported collapse.
What happened to the bridge?
Images published by Russian and Ukrainian Telegram channels, appear to show only one of the bridge's two arches remaining.
The channels reported that the other arch and part of the roadway had collapsed into the sea following the overnight attack.
Russia's Transport Ministry said the damage was being assessed but did not confirm the reported collapse.
The extent of the structural damage has not been independently verified.
Why the Crimean Bridge matters
The 19-kilometre Crimean Bridge connects Russia's Krasnodar Krai region with the Russian-occupied Crimean peninsula across the Kerch Strait.
Constructed after Russia's illegal annexation of Crimea in 2014, the $4 billion project opened to road traffic in 2018, with passenger rail services beginning in 2019.
The bridge serves as a critical military supply and transport route for Russian forces operating in occupied territories in southern Ukraine, facilitating the movement of military equipment, supplies and personnel.
It also holds enormous symbolic significance for Vladimir Putin, who championed its construction as a way of cementing Russia's control over Crimea following the annexation, one of the defining moments of his presidency.
The bridge has repeatedly been targeted by Ukrainian forces, suffering significant damage in October 2022 and July 2023, although neither attack permanently put it out of commission.
Zelenskyy described the latest operation as a response to Russia's continued attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure, including bridges in Kyiv, Zaporizhzhia, Dnipro and the Odesa region.
"We have repeatedly offered Russia steps toward de-escalation – and every proposal has been met with loud rejection," he said.
"Ukraine’s defensive capabilities are strong and will remain so, and we will never leave terror against our cities and people unanswered."

sources.title: Ukraine Attacks Kerch Bridge Linking Russia to Occupied Crimea
sources.text:
Supported by
Russia and Ukraine Trade Strikes Against Key Bridges
The attacks, far from the front lines, forced the only bridge between Russia and the occupied Crimean Peninsula to close. Traffic on two bridges in Kyiv was also stopped.
The only bridge linking Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula was temporarily closed on Tuesday morning after suffering damage from a series of Ukrainian attacks, according to Russian officials.
Overnight, two of the main bridges over the Dnipro River in Kyiv, Ukraine’s capital, were also temporarily closed after Russian strikes on the structures late on Monday, Ukrainian officials said.
The dual strikes on important bridges hundreds of miles from the front lines were part of a long-running battle in Russia’s war against Ukraine, involving logistics, symbols and survival. Bridges are some of the hardest structures to bring down using long-range weapons and such structures have repeatedly defied quick destruction.
The extent of the damage to the Ukrainian and Russian bridges was not immediately clear as engineering teams on both sides were dispatched to assess the aftermath of the attacks.
The Kerch Strait Bridge between Russia and Crimea, a 12-mile span that holds both military and political significance for the Kremlin, suffered structural damage, according to Russia’s Investigative Committee, the country’s equivalent of the F.B.I.
The Russian Transport Ministry said in a statement that road and rail traffic on the bridge had been suspended while inspections were conducted.
“Motorists are advised not to travel toward the Crimean Bridge and to monitor the operational situation in official sources,” the ministry said.
Russia illegally annexed Crimea from Ukraine in 2014, and Kyiv has repeatedly attacked the Kerch Strait Bridge since Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022. Ukrainian forces have tried, unsuccessfully, to take the bridge down in unconventional sabotage operations and by direct bombardments.
In October 2022, a truck bombing collapsed sections of the bridge and ignited a passing fuel train. Ukrainian forces followed up with a naval drone strike in July 2023 that damaged the road deck. In June 2025, Ukraine carried out an underwater demolition operation in which operatives detonated more than a metric ton of explosives against the bridge’s submerged support pillars.
Kyiv’s mayor, Vitali Klitschko, said on Tuesday that the capital’s Northern and Southern bridges were closed to traffic after the Russian missile attack Monday night.
“We will provide updates as soon as new information becomes available. Municipal services are working on the ground,” Mr. Klitschko said in a statement. “We are doing everything possible to restore traffic as quickly as possible.”
Marc Santora has been reporting from Ukraine since the beginning of the war with Russia. He was previously based in London as an international news editor focused on breaking news events and earlier the bureau chief for East and Central Europe, based in Warsaw. He has also reported extensively from Iraq and Africa.

slide.titolo: Attacco iraniano contro una base aerea americana
slide.testo: Secondo il Financial Times, l'Iran ha attaccato una base aerea degli Stati Uniti in Bahrein. È un attacco diretto contro una struttura militare americana nel Golfo.
Secondo i Pasdaran, il Corpo delle Guardie della rivoluzione islamica (IRGC), sono state colpite anche due navi cisterna di carburante nello Stretto di Hormuz.
L'attacco alle petroliere è riportato sulla base di quanto afferma l'IRGC. Dalle fonti disponibili non risultano conferme indipendenti.

slide.titolo: Vittime, danni e risposta USA: nessun dettaglio
slide.testo: Le fonti disponibili non indicano vittime, entità dei danni, nomi delle navi colpite né una reazione di Washington. Sono gli elementi da seguire nelle prossime ore.

c.perche_ti_riguarda: Hormuz è una rotta del carburante, come mostrano le petroliere colpite. Se la tensione si allarga, può farsi sentire sui prezzi dell'energia, quindi su bollette e carburanti anche in Italia.
